title: Quickstart
content: --- title: Quickstart --- Luma is a better way to write Python documentation. It's a modern replacement for Sphinx that's built on the same tooling Stripe uses for their documentation. Key benefits of Luma: - Markdown-native. Avoid Sphinx’s obscure syntax. - Built for Python. API generation and cros

title: Add a page
content: Pages are for general prose in your documentation, used to cover topics beyond auto-generated API references. To add a page, create a Markdown file in your folder. Then, specify the path in . You can also specify files in subdirectories. By default, Luma uses the first heading as the page's title in

title: Add an API reference
content: API references are automatically generated and document specific Python functions and classes. To add a reference, specify a in and list the APIs you want to include in that reference.

title: Add social media icons
content: Social media icons are the small links to your profiles shown in your doc's footer. By default, Luma doesn't display any social links. To add social media icons, specify the field in the top level of your config. You can specify GitHub, Discord, Twitter, or Slack.

title: Customize the favicon
content: Favicons are the small images shown on browser tabs and bookmarks. By default, Luma uses the Luma logo as a favicon. To use a different favicon, place an file in your project directory and specify it in your config.

title: Group pages in the sidenav
content: Sections allow you to group related pages and API references in the sidebar. To add a section, specify a in .

title: Publish your docs
content: Join our Discord to acquire an API key. Then, run the command to publish your documentation. After a minute, your documentation will be accessible at .
